stories.head: AI is raising customer expectations while tolerance for failure drops
stories.plain: Research shows that as AI-powered service becomes the norm, customers expect faster, more accurate responses — but are quicker to churn when the AI fails or blocks access to a human. This changes how marketers must design automated customer journeys, balancing speed with clear escalation paths.

stories.head: B2B marketing's real gap is evidence, not ROI
stories.plain: The argument here is that B2B marketers can't prove marketing's value because they lack connected data across the buyer journey, not because the returns aren't there. Fixing this means linking CDP-level identity data to revenue outcomes — a foundational shift in how marketing AI is governed and measured.

stories.head: Constructor reports 900% growth in AI agent customers
stories.plain: Constructor, a product discovery platform, says its AI agent customer base grew 900% year-over-year, signalling rapid enterprise adoption of agentic search and merchandising tools. That pace matters for buyers evaluating how fast the vendor landscape is shifting and which players are gaining real traction.

stories.head: Experiential retail media emerges as a new in-store AI frontier
stories.plain: The piece makes the case that physical retail aisles are the next high-value media channel, combining AI-driven personalization with in-store sensing and display. For MarTech buyers, this signals new investment in real-time decisioning at the shelf edge, where agentic and CDP capabilities must connect to physical touchpoints.

stories.head: Nextview joins Anthropic's Claude network amid B2B AI agent expansion
stories.plain: Nextview's entry into the Claude partner network is notable because it signals how B2B MarTech vendors are embedding foundation-model relationships into their stacks. Joining an approved model network affects which AI capabilities a vendor can offer and how governance obligations flow down to end customers.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams via Acquisition of DoubleO.ai
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and launched Agent Teams — coordinated AI agents that run full go-to-market plays from signal to closed action without human hand-holding at each step. This matters because it shifts B2B revenue tooling from AI-assisted to fully agentic, changing how marketing and sales software is bought and evaluated.

stories.head: Salesforce Acquires AI Customer Research Startup Listen Labs
stories.plain: Salesforce bought Listen Labs, which uses AI to conduct customer interviews, analyze responses, and simulate buyer behavior. Plugging this into Salesforce's CRM and AI agents means synthetic customer insight can feed directly into automated decisioning — raising new questions about data quality and governance at scale.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust™ Ecosystem for Continuous Intent Verification in Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: Experian and DataDome are building infrastructure to verify not just who an AI agent represents, but whether its actions stay within what it was authorized to do mid-transaction. This is foundational governance plumbing for agentic commerce — without it, autonomous purchasing at scale carries major fraud and liability risk.

stories.head: Braze Expands AI from Content Creation to Campaign Operations
stories.plain: Braze added AI decisioning tools, automated campaign health checks, and connections to external LLMs like Claude — moving it from a content-generation helper to a platform that automates operational choices inside live campaigns. This widens the gap between basic ESPs and modern CEPs, reshaping how marketers evaluate engagement platforms.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Radically Different 'AI Shelves,' Upending Brand and Price Competition
stories.plain: New Jellyfish data shows AI shopping assistants surface completely different product sets than traditional search, making established brand rankings and price positions unreliable. Brandtech is launching a 'Share of Model' optimization service to help marketers track and influence what AI recommends — a direct call to act on generative engine visibility.

themes.head: AI Raises the Expectation Floor While Lowering Tolerance for Failure
body: Customers who have experienced AI-powered speed and personalisation now hold every brand interaction to that standard — and forgive far less when it falls short. The gap between what AI promises and what most marketing execution actually delivers is becoming a competitive liability, not just a quality issue.

At the same time, analysts warn that AI made marketing faster before it made it better: volume went up, but relevance and trust did not automatically follow. Brands that close this gap by focusing on outcome quality — not output quantity — will define the next benchmark.

themes.head: The AI Search Rewrite Demands a New Visibility Playbook
body: Generative engines are dissolving the rules marketers spent a decade learning about SEO: click-through logic, keyword ranking, and even brand-size advantages no longer behave as expected. New Jellyfish research shows AI shopping is already upending price positioning and brand leadership in ways that legacy search never did.

Practitioners must now build visual SEO strategies, optimise for generative engine models, and debunk myths — such as the assumption that big brands automatically win in AI results — before their budgets follow the wrong map. This is one of the fastest-moving strategic pivots in the feed.

themes.head: Agentic AI Creates an Accountability Gap in GTM Operations
body: As autonomous AI agents proliferate across go-to-market stacks — from ZoomInfo's Agent Teams to DataDome's intent-verification layer — organisations are discovering they have no coherent way to audit what those agents are actually doing or deciding. The risk is not that agents underperform; it is that no one knows when they do.

The response is emerging as a governance layer: IBM's self-hosted AI sovereignty tooling, Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem, and rising demand for continuous intent verification all signal that trust infrastructure will become as important as the agents themselves. Teams that build oversight now will avoid costly clean-ups later.

themes.head: Retail & Commerce Media Enter an AI-Managed, Experience-First Era
body: Retail media is splitting into two tracks: automated AI management of performance-driven placements (CommerceIQ on Chewy Ads, Particular Audience's trade media) and a push toward in-store experiential formats that justify premium brand spend. The holiday retail calendar's collapse into year-round peaks is accelerating both pressures simultaneously.

For decision-makers, the implication is structural: separate budgets, KPIs, and agency briefs will increasingly be needed for the algorithmic efficiency layer versus the experiential brand layer. Treating retail media as a single channel is now a strategic mistake.

themes.head: B2B Stacks Shift From Data Collection to Evidence and Revenue Proof
body: The B2B marketing conversation has moved from 'do we have enough data?' to 'can we prove causality to the CFO?' MarTech argues the sector's ROI crisis is really an evidence crisis — CRM data sits idle while pipeline attribution remains fuzzy. Platforms like Growth7 and the AI-shaped buyer journey guide from Circle & Square both aim directly at this gap.

The CFO is now a primary audience for marketing technology decisions, as illustrated by Hyphenate's rebrand expanding explicitly 'across the Office of the CFO.' Marketers who cannot translate activity into credible revenue evidence will lose budget authority to finance teams that can.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack, the defining pressure of this month is the same: AI has moved fast enough to outpace the governance, evidence, and quality standards needed to make it trustworthy — and the brands that close that gap first will own the next cycle of customer & budget confidence.
